items.readable_text:
Content:
Whenever we write a decimal as a mixed number, our mixed number will have

Content:
- a whole number part corresponding to the decimal's whole number part, and
- a fractional part corresponding to the decimal part.

Content:
For example, let's write the following decimal as a mixed number:

Content:
[MATH: {\color{blue}{5.}}{\color{red}{7}}]

Content:
To express this decimal as a mixed number, we look at its whole number and decimal parts:

Content:
- The whole number part is [MATH: {\color{blue}5}.]
- The decimal part has [MATH: 1] decimal place. Therefore, we can write it as a decimal fraction as follows:
[MATH: 0.{\color{red}7} = \dfrac{\color{red}7}{10}]

Content:
Therefore, we express our decimal as a mixed number in the following way:

Content:
[MATH: {\color{blue}5}\,\dfrac{\color{red}7}{10}]

Whenever we write a decimal as a mixed number, our mixed number will have

  • a fractional part that corresponds to the decimal part to the right of the decimal point.

With that in mind, let's write [MATH: {\color{blue}1}.\!{\color{red}9}] as a mixed number.

  • The whole number part is [MATH: {\color{blue}1}.]

  • The decimal part has [MATH: 1] decimal place, so we can write it as a fraction in the following way: [MATH: 0.9 = {\color{red}\dfrac{9}{10}}]

Therefore, we can write the given decimal as the following mixed number:

[MATH: 1.9 = 1\,\dfrac{9}{10}]
